I will keep my land split across all three crops, but I will put the largest share into sweetpotato because that is the main cropping system I rely on and it fits how I manage risk and labor. I have 20 years of farming behind me, I have well irrigation, and my household is not large, so I will avoid anything too complicated and stay with a practical input level that I know I can carry through. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield on the better land and it responds well when I give it enough fertilizer and a few irrigations. For millet, I will keep inputs lower because it is more tolerant and gives me a steadier crop on lighter management. For sweetpotato, I will use improved planting material, keep nitrogen moderate so vines do not grow too wild, and give more potassium because that helps tuber formation. I will use rotary tillage on most of the land because it is easier for me to manage at this scale, and I will keep pesticide use moderate, only enough to protect yield. My overall approach this year is to balance output, labor, and cost, not to chase the highest possible yield with the highest possible risk.
